services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java (added in this PR): the Javadoc on `void requireView()` says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}', but the method returns void. Same file, ClientPermissionEvaluator.java: the Javadoc on `void requireViewClientScopes()` says 'Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}', but the method is void and, like its siblings, should be documented as 'Throws ForbiddenException if #canViewClientScopes() returns false'.

The two features can't both be enabled. common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/Profile.java:56,58: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (version 1) and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (version 2) share the unversioned key 'admin-fine-grained-authz' (constructor :162-163 strips the _V2 suffix). Profile.java:283-286 throws ProfileException('Multiple versions of the same feature ... should not be enabled'), so only one version is ever active. When the listener's v1 gate (AdminPermissions.java:77) is true, V2 is off, so management() (:66-71) returns plain MgmtPermissions and never ClientPermissionsV2. The new gate actually fixes the problem: before this PR the listener ran with no gate, so with V2 enabled it would have reached ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (:193), which throws.
